title: Close the residual command-classification gaps left after the A1 canonicalisation

It cannot see text that only exists at run time

title: Residual: an unrestricted same-user agent, and runs with no host permission prompt, can bypass any file-level or syntactic protection
impact: R-13 protects JADE's ledger, overlays, pins, calibration file and installed code as gated targets, but an agent with a shell as the same OS user can reach them by a route the classifier cannot read (a script it wrote first, a computed path, its own pty). In bypassPermissions/auto, headless and unattended subagent runs JADE's gate is the only gate
rationale: Permit rows carry no signature; an HMAC needs a key the agent cannot read, and a Keychain item readable by the same user does not qualify. This is an honest limit of a same-user hook gate, documented in docs/05 T18 and T19
next_action: Run unattended agents in a sandbox or as a separate OS user; decide whether to sign permit rows with a key held by a separate helper process or user
retry_or_revisit_trigger: first unattended or bypass-mode deployment, or first observed ledger tampering

title: Residual: a patch applied from a file or stdin, a symlink made in the same command, an agent-allocated pty and pyproject.toml are outside R-13/R-16
impact: `patch -p1 < p` and `git apply p` change protected files named only inside the patch; `ln -s ~/.claude /tmp/c && echo x > /tmp/c/settings.json` in one command writes through a link that does not exist when the gate looks; an agent that opens its own pty can satisfy is_human_tty; pyproject.toml (entry points, dependencies) is not a protected file because any project has one
rationale: A syntactic gate sees the command line, not the patch body, the filesystem after the command and not the process tree. The first pass closed the Write/Edit/redirect routes and the programmatic route (SI-09 on `from jade import cli`); these remain honest design limits (docs/05 T19)
next_action: Decide between (a) reading the patch for `+++ b/<path>` headers when it is a file or heredoc on the command line, (b) refusing is_human_tty when the controlling terminal's session leader is not a login shell or a terminal emulator, (c) an HMAC on permit rows keyed by a secret the agent cannot read (also W-34); measure would_block volume first
retry_or_revisit_trigger: first observed bypass, or the first unattended run in bypassPermissions
